people.gloss: The sound of rain on leaves (Tô Thức)
people.role: Head of Xuyên Lâm Môn since 1170: staff and footwork, guides through the rain forest; the Tower's chính vassal and its least willing one
people.appearance: A broad, weathered man in a straw cape with a bamboo staff worn pale at the grip, who walks everywhere and is never out of breath.
people.backstory: Úc Diệp Thanh was born in 970 at Thủ Lôi Bảo, the Tower's thunder fort on the ridge, where his father carried salt and barley up for the garrison. The ridge gave him Metal and Fire, the forest road gave him Wood, and the fort gave him Thunder, which no one at Xuyên Lâm Môn could teach. Nhậm Bình Sinh (nham_binh_sinh) took him at fourteen anyway and taught him to walk. In 1042 Phượng Minh burned the fort he was born in (V161). In 1156 his younger brother Úc Từ Hành (uc_tu_hanh) guided the Tower's column into Đan Sơn Mạch and stayed with its rear guard at the pass (N-thinh_vu-08). Ten years later the Tower put its new seat on Thần Cổ Phong, among the Gate's mines. His master sat nine days in the rain at the Tower's new gate in protest, came home and died (N-xuyen_lam-03). Úc became head in 1170 and guided every traveller himself for a year (A296), so that the forest would see whose road it was. That same year he sent his brother's son Úc Đả Diệp (uc_da_diep) to the Tower as surety (N-thinh_vu-11). In 1199 he planted the Gate's claim on the risen isle at Hà Châu (A297).
people.wants: His nephew home and the Gate out from under the Tower without a war; and, for himself, someone who can teach the Thunder in his root.
people.secret: Khúc Phụ Thạch's daughter passes him the dates of the Tower's storm drills. While the Tower's Thunder disciples are up on Liệt Khuyết Phong, he searches the Gate's mines for the door Hầu Xuân Lôi sealed in 470 (C035). He has heard drumming under Tử Tinh Khoáng, and he wants what is behind it for his own root, not for the Gate.

people.role: The Road Mother (Lộ Mẫu): master of the guides and keeper of the road books; holds the founder's straw cape
people.appearance: A small, bent woman under a cape so old its straw has gone silver, with a road book under one arm and a lamp in the other hand.
people.backstory: Phí Thoa Y was born in 905 at Dẫn Lộ Thôn, the guides' village in the bamboo below the gate, the year the Tower proclaimed the Night Rain Edict (C167). She carried packs on the forest road at eight and a lamp at twelve. Nhậm Bình Sinh (nham_binh_sinh) took her as his last disciple and gave her the road books: every crossing, ford, beast den and inn between the ridge and the sea. For two hundred years she has kept them, and the guides call her the Road Mother. In 976 she led a frightened girl from Hạnh Hoa Thị up the road to the Tower's gate. The girl was Ninh Tịch Đăng (ninh_tich_dang), now keeper of the Tower's lamps. In 1177 a Xuyên Lâm boy deserted the Tower and came down the road at night. Phí hid Nghiêm Quy Khứ (nghiem_quy_khu) in her own house and wrote one letter up the mountain. The boy's lamp was not put out. When their master died in 1169, he left the founder's staff to Úc Diệp Thanh (uc_diep_thanh) and the founder's cape to her. The Gate has read that as a division ever since. She thinks it was meant as a balance.
people.wants: To keep the road open and the Gate whole, to train a Road Mother after her, and to see the staff and the cape in one pair of hands before she dies. She no longer much minds whose hands they are.
people.secret: Hứa Thanh Diêm has written to her on the Rain Tower's behalf: if the Gate set Úc aside, the Tower would confirm her as head and send Úc Đả Diệp home. She has kept the letter for three years and not answered it.

people.role: The Tower's deserter of 1177, now a staff of the Gate; his life lamp still burns in the Tower's soul vaults
people.appearance: A quiet man with a bronze cup still hung at his throat, which he has never taken off.
people.backstory: Born below the gate in 1150, Nghiêm Quy Khứ passed the Tower's outer gate on his Metal and climbed the ridge in 1167. Ten years later he would not learn the Night Rain arts and walked home by night (N-thinh_vu-12). Lệ Tiêu Hồn (le_tieu_hon) wanted his lamp put out. Ninh Tịch Đăng (ninh_tich_dang) refused to cut the wick, and Phí Thoa Y (phi_thoa_y) hid him. He has taught the Gate's outer boys for twenty years. His sister went up the ridge in 1192 to find out why he lives.
people.wants: To die when his own lamp goes out, not when the Tower's shears close.
people.secret: He is teaching the outer boys a counting rhyme that is really the order of the Tower's lamp-shear cuts, so the Gate will know how to keep a lamp from the shears after him. Thôi Vọng Phàm (thoi_vong_pham) has learned the first verse and sells it to nobody yet.

people.role: Warden of the Gate's ferry post at Hà Châu, who planted its claim on the risen isle
people.appearance: A thick-armed ferryman with a staff that doubles as a pole and a gourd of rice wine that never seems to empty.
people.backstory: Đinh Vãn Độ was born at Hà Châu on the forest river in 1085 and has run the Gate's ferry there for ninety years. When the earthquake of 1199 raised an isle in the river beside his landing (A297), he poled out to it before the water had settled and drove the Gate's staff into its mud. The Tower claims it too, and its envoy Hứa Thanh Diêm (hua_thanh_diem) has come to say so twice. Úc Diệp Thanh (uc_diep_thanh) taught him the staff and has not told him to pull it out.
people.wants: The isle held in the Gate's name until the river changes again.
people.secret: He is poling Tower stone-cutters out to the isle by night for a skin of rice wine a trip, while swearing at its envoy Hứa Thanh Diêm (hua_thanh_diem) by day.

people.role: The head's last disciple and the fastest guide on the forest road; the Gate's courier to its hostage
people.appearance: Long-legged and sunburnt, with her sandals tied on with red thread and her staff across her shoulders like a yoke.
people.backstory: A guide's daughter from Dẫn Lộ Thôn who outran the head's own pack-boys at twelve. Úc Diệp Thanh (uc_diep_thanh) took her as his last disciple in 1170, the year he sent his nephew up the ridge. She has carried the Gate's letters to Úc Đả Diệp (uc_da_diep) every season since she was twenty, and her own with them. She teaches his daughter the staff, and the girl does not know why she is so patient with her.
people.wants: The hostage home, and one letter she may sign herself.
people.secret: She is cutting a path to the ridge for Úc Yên Vũ (uc_yen_vu) in case her holding the girl back fails, one bend a season, each marked with a bit of red thread.

people.role: Founder of Xuyên Lâm Môn (690); author of its primer and its staff canon
people.backstory: A forest guide born in Đả Diệp Lâm who walked the rain forest road with a bamboo staff, straw sandals and a straw cape, and paid the rain no attention. In 690 he gathered the guides and staff fighters of the road into a gate at the pass where the road leaves the ridge, and swore it to the Tower (A289). He wrote the Gate's primer and its canon, and he died on the road in 878, still guiding.

people.backstory: The founder's first disciple, who joined at eighteen in 690 and led the Gate for three hundred years. When the Tower opened to the ma đạo arts he refused them and walked the forest road alone for a month in protest (A292). In 1169 he sat nine days in the rain at the Tower's new gate on Thần Cổ Phong without a hat (N-xuyen_lam-03), walked home, and died that winter. He left the founder's staff to Úc Diệp Thanh (uc_diep_thanh) and the founder's cape to Phí Thoa Y (phi_thoa_y).
